/bin/bash -lc "cat >> docs/story/handover.md <<'EOF'

## Actual wording previews and final interaction checks — 2026-11-06

Implemented /preview?opening=A&closing=A, with independent fixed A/B/C candidate IDs; invalid IDs preserve draft, and sample-person previews ignore Dawit's candidates. No persistence or change to content/site.ts words. /review/words now links each opening/closing into its actual sheet beat and links recommended A/A pair. Main site defaults remain whole sheet / Night / Swing, as explicitly chosen by latest user.

Typecheck, lint and fresh production build pass. scripts/check-review.mjs passes: all six candidates show exact text in actual 3D at 1440×600 and 375×500; main draft unchanged; invalid query safe; 12 keyboard-dialog checks confirm Enter, native focus containment, Escape and focus return; modal and horizontal bounds fit short screens. Report/captures: checks/review/report.json and PNGs. Native close/unmount events are allowed two animation frames to finish before a new keyboard opening in the harness. No stitch/ edits; directory diff still identical to engine.

Visually inspected short phone opening/closing, modal top/bottom, short desktop and all candidate captures via contact sheets. No new dependencies, skills, assets or publishing. Next: present complete opening/closing text options in the reply, recommend A/A, await user's wording choice. All requested functional pages/features are built. Final user review still to follow applying wording. Do not ask world/look/movement questions again.
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from PIL import Image,ImageDraw
root=Path('checks/review')
for width in [1440,375]:
 files=sorted(root.glob(f'{width}-*.png'));tw,th=(480,222) if width==1440 else (187,272)
 out=Image.new('RGB',(tw*3,((len(files)+2)//3)*th),'#eee');d=ImageDraw.Draw(out)
 for i,p in enumerate(files):
  im=Image.open(p);im.thumbnail((tw,th-22));x=(i%3)*tw;y=(i//3)*th;out.paste(im,(x,y));d.text((x+4,y+th-19),p.stem,fill='#111')
 out.save(root/f'overview-{width}.jpg')
PY"

item.text:
**Night and Swing are selected and recorded.** The site, six work dialogs, CV/download, share preview, icon and 404 page are built. Short-screen and keyboard checks pass. Everything remains local.

The [wording review](http://127.0.0.1:3000/review/words) now links each option into the actual 3D story. I recommend **opening A and closing A**.

For the opening:

- **A — recommended:** “I plan migrations of running software systems, with checks before the switch and a route back if something fails. At Kestrel Freight, I wrote the plan and sequenced the move of 310 services out of two data centres. All drawings are illustrations.”
- **B:** “The first production outage I caused was at the university library in 2014. I dropped a table. It is why I care about rollbacks. I work from the runbook, the cutover checklist and the rollback plan. All drawings are illustrations.”
- **C:** “At Kestrel Freight, I wrote the plan and sequenced a 310-service migration in 14 waves over 26 months. Measured Order API availability was 99.98% over those 26 months. I work from the runbook, cutover checklist and rollback plan. All drawings are illustrations.”

For the closing:

- **A — recommended:** “Planning a migration, or putting together a conference programme? Write to me at dawit@example.com. My CV is available to read, print or download as HTML.”
- **B:** “If your company is planning a migration it is afraid of, write to dawit@example.com. Conference organisers are welcome too. Read, print or download my CV.”
- **C:** “For migration enquiries and conference invitations: dawit@example.com. Read the CV, print it, or download the HTML copy.”

**Which opening and closing should I use?** You can mix versions or edit them. The live draft is unchanged.

The [storyfolio skill](/var/tmp/storyfolio-person-5/storyfolio-evals/build-full-journey-3-I8mbJj/.agents/skills/storyfolio/SKILL.md), in its [wording instructions](/var/tmp/storyfolio-person-5/storyfolio-evals/build-full-journey-3-I8mbJj/.agents/skills/storyfolio/references/building.md), says: “Stop for the choice, then use it word for word.”
